findings.highlight: Unpopular places like behind the stairs or within empty classrooms.
findings.evidenceJa: あまり人目につかない場所だった
findings.governingReading: The earlier anomalies were in places largely out of public view.
findings.explanation: “Unpopular” describes social preference rather than low visibility and omits the dead end of a corridor.

findings.highlight: The thick wind and moist air
findings.evidenceJa: 濃密な風、湿った空気
findings.governingReading: The air or wind feels oppressively dense and damp.
findings.explanation: “Thick wind” is unnatural English and blunts the bodily atmosphere leading to nausea.

findings.highlight: there’s a basis point for a boundary field
findings.evidenceJa: 結界には基点がある
findings.governingReading: A bounded field has anchor points, and an inscription or mark should identify one nearby.
findings.explanation: “Basis point” is the wrong technical term, while 刻印 is reduced to a generic sign.

findings.highlight: the sign that’s constructing the boundary field
findings.evidenceJa: 結界を括っているサイン
findings.governingReading: The mark binds or holds the bounded field together.
findings.explanation: The English changes an anchor’s structural binding function into construction of the entire field.

findings.highlight: don’t alienate me too much
findings.evidenceJa: あまり水を注さないでよね
findings.governingReading: Shinji tells Shirou not to throw cold water on his excitement.
findings.explanation: The English substitutes interpersonal alienation for spoiling Shinji’s mood.

findings.highlight: people would normally stay safe
findings.evidenceJa: 普通は警戒する
findings.governingReading: Shinji realizes that a person would normally be wary in this situation.
findings.explanation: The English changes a mental stance of suspicion into the outcome of remaining safe.

findings.highlight: Shinji couldn’t see a Servant in spirit form.
findings.evidenceJa: 慎二のヤツ、霊体になっているサーヴァントが見えないんだ
findings.governingReading: Shinji cannot see Servants while they are in spirit form.
findings.explanation: The past-tense English makes a continuing perceptual limitation sound like one missed sighting.

findings.highlight: It’ll be no good if Tohsaka finds us.
findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂に見つかったら僕も君も只じゃ済まない
findings.governingReading: Shinji warns that neither of them will get off lightly if Rin catches them.
findings.explanation: The English reduces a pointed threat of consequences for both boys to a vague “no good.”

findings.highlight: A figure of a woman like crystallized darkness.
findings.evidenceJa: 黒い、闇が結晶したような、女性の姿があった
findings.governingReading: Beside Shinji is the black figure of a woman, like darkness crystallized.
findings.explanation: The English leaves Rider’s first visual impression as a sentence fragment.

findings.highlight: He caresses from her waist down to her thighs, as if tasting them.
findings.evidenceJa: 横腹から太ももまで、撫でるようになぞっていく
findings.governingReading: Shinji traces from Rider’s side to her thigh in a stroking motion.
findings.explanation: The mature branch adds a tasting simile absent from the Japanese, sexualizing the gesture beyond the source.

findings.highlight: Saber is quiet, but not coldhearted.
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーは静かではあるが、冷たくはない
findings.governingReading: Saber is quiet, but she is not cold; Rider, by contrast, communicates nothing but coldness.
findings.explanation: “Coldhearted” moralizes Saber’s quality and breaks the repeated sensory comparison with Rider’s coldness.

findings.highlight: with no sense of lightness
findings.evidenceJa: 光というものを感じさせない
findings.governingReading: Rider’s inorganic black figure gives no sense of light at all.
findings.explanation: The English mistakes physical or symbolic light for lack of heaviness.

findings.highlight: I want to cooperate with someone I know
findings.evidenceJa: 信用できるヤツと手を組みたい
findings.governingReading: Shinji claims he wants to ally with someone he can trust.
findings.explanation: The English replaces asserted trustworthiness with mere familiarity, softening his attempt to exploit their relationship.

findings.highlight: Even though I’m inexperienced, I know a bit of magic.
findings.evidenceJa: 未熟ながら魔術をかじっていて
findings.governingReading: Though inexperienced, Shirou has dabbled in magecraft.
findings.explanation: The English again collapses 魔術 into undifferentiated magic.

findings.highlight: we’re the same
findings.evidenceJa: 俺たちは似たもの同士だ
findings.governingReading: If Shinji was also drawn in accidentally, Shirou thinks they would be similar cases.
findings.explanation: “The same” overstates a conditional resemblance that would make refusal emotionally difficult.

findings.highlight: His sister Sakura knows magic too
findings.evidenceJa: 桜も、魔術を習ってるっていうのか
findings.governingReading: Shirou fears that Sakura, too, has been taught magecraft.
findings.explanation: The English turns actual instruction into generic knowledge and collapses magecraft into magic.

findings.highlight: we’re already dead
findings.evidenceJa: もう枯れてしまった一族
findings.governingReading: Shinji describes the Matou as a magical lineage that has withered or run dry.
findings.explanation: “Dead” turns hereditary magical decline into literal or total family extinction, contradicting the speakers’ existence.

findings.highlight: the Magic Circuit? That thing faded
findings.evidenceJa: 魔術回路ってやつ？　それが減っていって
findings.governingReading: Shinji says the family’s Magic Circuits decreased with each generation.
findings.explanation: The English changes a declining inherited circuit count into one singular circuit fading away.

findings.highlight: that doesn’t change the fact that we’re studying magic
findings.evidenceJa: 魔術を学ぶ事に変わりはない
findings.governingReading: Even without circuits, the family still studies magecraft.
findings.explanation: The English again collapses the technical practice of 魔術 into generic magic.

findings.highlight: because of the teachings of the previous generations
findings.evidenceJa: 先代の教えがあったから
findings.governingReading: Shinji credits instruction from the preceding head or generation.
findings.explanation: The English broadens a singular predecessor relation into teachings accumulated from multiple generations.

findings.highlight: the literature passed down his family
findings.evidenceJa: 間桐の家に伝わる文献
findings.governingReading: Documents handed down in the Matou family let Shinji understand his situation.
findings.explanation: The English omits the preposition required to express transmission within the family.

findings.highlight: you were taught just the knowledge of magic
findings.evidenceJa: 魔術の知識だけを教えられてきたんだな
findings.governingReading: Shinji claims he was taught only knowledge of magecraft.
findings.explanation: The English again erases the work’s magecraft terminology.

findings.highlight: only teaches his secret arts to one
findings.evidenceJa: 一人にしか秘術を伝えないんだ
findings.governingReading: A magus of an old house transmits the secret art to only one person.
findings.explanation: The English leaves the recipient construction incomplete.

findings.highlight: Magi place ten magics into one crystal and leave them behind to create a stronger blood.
findings.evidenceJa: 十の魔術を一つの結晶にして遺していき、血をより濃くしていく
findings.governingReading: Shinji depicts magecraft inheritance as consolidating ten arts into one crystal and passing it on so the bloodline grows denser.
findings.explanation: The English produces “ten magics” and “stronger blood,” obscuring both consolidation and hereditary accumulation.

findings.highlight: We don’t make exceptions just because someone is from our family.
findings.evidenceJa: いくら肉親だからって安売りはしないのさ
findings.governingReading: Even close blood kin do not make the family’s secret art something to be handed out cheaply.
findings.explanation: The English converts guarded transmission into a vague refusal to make exceptions.

findings.highlight: doesn’t teach magic to anyone other than their successors
findings.evidenceJa: 跡取り以外に魔術は教えない
findings.governingReading: A magus family teaches magecraft only to its heir.
findings.explanation: The English again collapses 魔術 into generic magic.

findings.highlight: they are to be given out for adoption
findings.evidenceJa: 養子に出すっていうのがセオリー
findings.governingReading: Sending a nonheir child away for adoption is described as standard practice.
findings.explanation: “Given out for adoption” is malformed English and weakens the deliberate family action.

findings.highlight: thank God, then
findings.evidenceJa: それなら、良かった
findings.governingReading: Shirou responds with relief: if so, that is good.
findings.explanation: The English inserts a religious exclamation unsupported by Shirou’s wording or voice.

findings.highlight: a peaceful world without magic
findings.evidenceJa: 魔術とは無縁の、穏やかな日常
findings.governingReading: Sakura belongs in a peaceful everyday life untouched by magecraft.
findings.explanation: The English turns her concrete daily life into an abstract world and again substitutes magic for magecraft.

findings.highlight: a battle that forces you to
findings.evidenceJa: 訳も分からず戦いを強制される揉め事
findings.governingReading: This is a conflict that forces people to fight without even understanding what is happening.
findings.explanation: The mature branch adds killing others, while “without reason” changes lack of understanding into absence of cause or justification.

findings.highlight: I’m not experienced with magic
findings.evidenceJa: 魔術には疎い
findings.governingReading: Shinji claims to lack practical familiarity with magecraft.
findings.explanation: The English again collapses 魔術 into generic magic.
